audit_scope: Post-hoc source review of rejected_candidates indices 0, 1, 2, and 9 only. These are not emitted detector findings and are not a recall estimate.
execution: Read source and git history only; no corpus code, tests, builds, registry requests, or detector changes.

cases.reason: The fix passes a PackageKey into the recorded-input checker to resolve peer ownership in new lockfiles. The surviving function is deliberately the compatibility path for old entries without specifiers; it calls a different child checker. Its source explicitly says it takes no new fixes and will be removed at the next lockfile major.
cases.structural_rejection: different_function_signature; destructured Rust parameter fallback keeps literal identifiers

evidence.observation: Dispatches entries with specifiers to check_recorded_directory and others to check_legacy_directory; the legacy-path comment states its maintenance policy.
Requires PackageKey and calls check_recorded_local_targets with (snapshot, key).
Legacy path calls check_local_dep_children_freshness, then its own peer freshness check.

cases.reason: The fixed reader fetches a whole package document before mutation and requests its current revision. The surviving reader fetches a dist-tag map from a separate endpoint. Tag mutations use direct PUT/DELETE requests and do not write back a fetched package revision. Similar HTTP/error-handling scaffolding does not establish a shared freshness requirement.
cases.structural_rejection: different_function_signature; generic package metadata versus BTreeMap<String, String> and distinct context/error types

evidence.observation: Fixed package reader adds ?write=true; comment explains current revision before package-document mutation.
Survivor fetches and deserializes a dist-tag map.
Writes directly to /-/package/<package>/dist-tags/<tag>; list reads use /-/package/<package>/dist-tags. No package-document revision is read then written.

cases.reason: The legacy star/unstar path performs the same package-document read-modify-write operation affected by the revision-freshness fix. It still fetches the plain package URL, changes users, and PUTs the full document using its fetched _rev. The stricter matcher discards this review lead because helper parameters and return types differ, despite the similar mutation contract.
cases.structural_rejection: different_function_signature; deprecation takes (FetchFromRegistry, PackageMetaRequest), star takes (LegacyStarActionArgs, string), with different return types and destructuring fallback

evidence.observation: Fixed helper GETs ?write=true before changing version deprecation fields and PUTting the package document.
Legacy fallback is reachable after supported modern-endpoint errors; it GETs without write=true, edits users, and PUTs the full document at /-rev/<fetched revision> when present.
Shared fetch passes the caller's URL through; fullMetadata selects the Accept header, not a write=true query.
Existing legacy-star test mocks a plain /foo GET and one fixed revision; it does not exercise stale versus current registry revisions. Read only, not executed.

limits: Source-supported review lead, not a reproduced bug.
Modern star endpoints avoid the package-document fallback.
Actual stale-read behavior and write=true support of registries using the legacy fallback were not tested.

cases.reason: The new emptySideEffects check feeds a new global-virtual-store decision distinguishing an empty cache row from no row. That distinction tells an already placed shared slot to stage a build for effects outside the package. The hoisted importer has no shared-slot placement shortcut or getCacheRow consumer: it always imports the fetched package and uses the cache key only for file maps. Propagating this local key-generation change alone has no corresponding hoisted behavior to fix.
cases.structural_rejection: different_function_signature; PackageImportContext versus ImportPkgContext and different argument layout

evidence.observation: Recognizes emptySideEffects, calculates a cache key, then calls getCacheRow and selectImportDir.
An empty row causes a previously placed slot to stage another build for outside effects. No staging token returns the regular package directory.
Survivor's caller always imports; it has no getCacheRow/selectImportDir placement decision.
Cache keys without an associated sideEffectsMaps entry do not change the imported file map or isBuilt result.

limits: Judgment concerns propagation of this emitted edit, not a blanket claim that all empty-cache or hoisted build behavior is correct.
